lesson.title: Exploring Punjab: Land of Five Rivers
lesson.subject: social-studies

contentBlocks.text: Today we travel (on the map!) to a real place: Punjab, a region in South Asia. Its name gives you a clue about its geography before you even learn anything else.

Punjab is a region in South Asia, on the continent of Asia. Its name comes from words meaning 'five rivers' — historically, five rivers (the Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab, and Jhelum) flow through the wider Punjab region. Today, Punjab is divided between two countries: India and Pakistan, each with a Punjab region of its own. All that water makes the land very fertile — Punjab grows huge amounts of wheat and rice, so much that it's often called a 'breadbasket,' a place that produces enough food to feed far more people than live there. Find Asia on a world map or globe, and if you can, locate India and Pakistan.
You just learned real geography about Punjab: its name, its rivers, and why it's such an important farming region. Tomorrow we'll compare Punjab's community and culture to your own.

objectives: Locate Punjab and South Asia on a map
Explain why Punjab is called 'land of five rivers' and why that makes it strong farmland
materialsNeeded: A world map, atlas, or globe (a printed map image also works)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Introduce Punjab's name meaning ('five rivers') as a geography clue.
2. Locate Asia, then South Asia, then India and Pakistan on a map together.
3. Discuss how the five rivers make the land fertile, and what 'breadbasket' means.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's comparison between the child's own community and a Punjab community.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus only on 'Punjab has lots of rivers, so its farms grow lots of food' without requiring the five rivers to be named individually
Ready for more: research one specific crop Punjab is known for growing and why the climate/rivers support it
Scoped deliberately to geography only this lesson — Punjab's history and the story of the Sikh Panth are covered in the Sikhi course, not duplicated here
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. Punjab means 'land of five rivers.' 2. Punjab is located in South Asia, divided between India and Pakistan. 3. Punjab is called a 'breadbasket' because its fertile, well-watered land produces huge amounts of wheat and rice.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Builds real geographic knowledge of South Asia/Punjab (C3 Framework Geography dimension) as a factual foundation before Day 4's cultural comparison — deliberately scoped to geography/agriculture, not history, which the Sikhi course covers separately.
